comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
## Evaluation: does the prod_impact floor ("Fix 2") run counter to the novelty convergence floor?

**Verdict: YES — the concern is accurate, and it is structural, not merely a tuning collision.
Fix 2 is rejected.**

### The mechanism

The rising floor (ADR-0008, `decide.rising_floor_drop`, wired at
`plan_review/__init__.py:109`) is what makes the remediation loop converge. Its drop predicate:

```
DROP iff novelty >= t_novel AND priority < floor
```

with `novelty_drop_threshold = 0.7` and **`novelty_priority_floor = 0.4`**
(`_config_schema.py:299-300`). The four quadrants matter: only *novel + low-priority* drops.
Carryover findings are always kept; novel + high-priority is kept because it may be a real
defect the plan edit introduced.

Convergence therefore depends entirely on **`priority < 0.4`** being a large, stable set. It
is: **13,337 of 18,085 plan-v3 findings (73.7%) sit below 0.4**, and **8,632 (47.7%) are at
priority exactly 0.0** — precisely because all seven axes are `none`. The zero-impact
population that Fix 2 targets *is* the convergence reservoir.

### Why Fix 2 collides and Fix 1 does not

Fix 2 raises impact for a population defined by an axis (`prod_impact`) that is **orthogonal to
whether the finding is novel or carryover**. It lifts findings across 0.4 based on a property
that has nothing to do with the remediation loop, so novel findings that would have been
dropped for convergence now survive *and* can block. Measured escape from the floor-eligible
population:

| change | findings crossing the 0.4 novelty floor | % of floor-eligible pop |
|---|---|---|
| Fix 2 @ prod floor 0.60 | 545 | 4.09% |
| Fix 2 @ prod floor 0.70 | 666 | 4.99% |
| Fix 2 @ prod floor 0.85 | 735 | 5.51% |
| **Fix 1 (divergence-graded)** | **357** | **2.68%** |

Fix 2 at the floor value it actually needs (0.70 — anything lower does not catch the target
finding) removes **~1.9x** as much convergence headroom as Fix 1.

The qualitative difference is the decisive part. Fix 1 lifts a **semantically bounded** class:
the plan misdescribes or under-scopes reality. That class is *inherently* remediable — the
author adds the site, the next review scores it `none`, and the finding legitimately
disappears. The loop still terminates. Fix 2 lifts an **unbounded severity band**:
"anything with medium+ production impact." A plan author cannot make `prod_impact: medium`
go away by editing the plan, because it describes the consequence, not the plan text. So a
Fix-2-lifted finding can recur at high priority across every remediation round with no author
action that resolves it — exactly the non-terminating loop the rising floor exists to prevent.

There is also a second, independent collision. Plan-v3 deliberately pinned
`UNDERSPECIFIED_ORACLE_CONTRIB = 0.55` *strictly below* every blocking threshold (0.60), with
a test that fails loudly if a recalibration violates it. A 0.70 `prod_impact` floor would score
a bare "medium production impact" finding **above** an underspecified oracle — inverting an
ordering that calibration 3 established on measured evidence.

### Why rejecting Fix 2 costs little

Fix 1 subsumes most of Fix 2's value. Of the 77 findings Fix 2 would newly block at 0.70, 20
(26%) are literal textual matches for Fix 1's omitted-scope class. Reading the residual 57 by
hand, the large majority are *also* divergence in substance — "plan says `finalize_verdict`
takes a new key, but `orchestrator.py:497` only checks X", "plan targets
`_LOCAL_TO_JIRA_STATUS` but `jira_fields.py` holds independent copies", "plan asserts the
migration is safe but `completion_verifier.md:59` contradicts it for epics". These are
`contradicts_reality` and `omits_required_site` under the new grading; my regex simply did not
match their phrasing. So Fix 1's semantic grading reaches them, while Fix 2's severity band was
only ever a blunt proxy for the same signal.

### Recommendation

Ship Fix 1 alone. If a residual gap survives plan-v4 dogfooding, the right follow-up is another
*semantic* axis grade (or a new axis), not a production-severity floor — the loop-termination
property above is a hard constraint on any future impact change, and worth stating in the gate
doc so the next calibration does not rediscover it.

## Review-loop trail (the gate reviewing its own calibration change)

Three `review-plan` runs so far; the gate has been genuinely useful on its own change. Recording
because the pattern is itself calibration evidence.

**Run 1 — BLOCK, 4 blocking / 9 advisory / 7 dropped.** Three of the four (E4, G6, T8) independently
found the SAME real gap: the plan said "mirror the oracle-kind precedent exactly" but never stated
that `divergent_implementation` must be excluded from `_SEV01`. Since `_SEV01` is keyed only on
`none|low|medium|high`, a schema-only change would have scored all three new symbolic grades as
`0.0` — the axis would have stopped firing ENTIRELY rather than flooring, i.e. the exact inverse of
the intent. The implementation already did this correctly; the PLAN text did not say so, and the
plan is the artifact under review. Fixed by naming the four structural changes explicitly.
The fourth (E2) caught real ambiguity: AC8's "may clear" left mandatory-vs-discretionary
undetermined; now stated as MUST/MUST NOT with the exact post-attestation value asserted.

Notable: those three fired via `vague_directive: high`, NOT via the divergence axis — the reviewer
classified "the plan doesn't say to bypass `_SEV01`" as vagueness rather than divergence. Worth
watching post-landing whether `omits_required_site` starts absorbing this class, since it is
arguably the better home for it.

**Run 2 — BLOCK, 3 blocking / 13 advisory / 8 dropped.** Two findings named UNENUMERATED CONSUMERS
holding ordinal-graded fixtures that the Literal would turn into parse errors:
- `tests/unit/test_a8e5_operator_attested_edge.py` — caught by the unit suite (1 failure).
- `tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_plan_review_gate.py:1282` — **NOT** in `tests/unit`, so the unit
  suite was green while this would have failed CI. This is precisely the `omits_required_site`
  class: a site the change provably must touch, absent from the declared scope. The gate caught a
  real break the fast test loop could not.
Third finding (T8) caught a pink-elephant: the verifiers' shared preamble said "Grade each axis
none|low|medium|high (EXCEPT ac_unverifiable...)", which would actively fight the new grades. Both
preambles now name BOTH kind-graded axes.

**Run 3 — BLOCK, 2 blocking / 10 advisory / 11 dropped.** One stale (it re-flagged
`test_impact_plan.py` ordinal uses already migrated in run 2 — the reviewer read pre-revision text).
One REAL and new: `plan_review_G7.md` is a prompt-side consumer that states it "maps its severity
onto the existing `divergent_implementation` plan axis" but named no grade — it would have kept
emitting `low`/`medium`/`high` into an axis that no longer accepts them. Fixed by giving G7 an
explicit kind mapping. Its eval spec references the axis in prose only (no asserted grade), so it
needs no change.

**Verification status at this point:** `make lint` clean, `make typecheck` clean (381 files),
`pytest tests/unit` 5,580 passed / 19 skipped / 0 failed, `pytest tests/interfaces/lifecycle/
test_plan_review_gate.py` 88 passed. All touched `src/rebar` files under the 800-LOC cap
(largest: `workflow_ops.py` at 785).

## ADR-0054 §3(a) corpus replay — the pre-landing bound (zero LLM calls)

Practising what ADR 0054 mandates, on this very change. Because a grade-set change alters what the
Pass-2 verifier EMITS, replay cannot predict the outcome — it can only BRACKET it. So the corpus was
re-scored twice through the real `impact_plan` + `pass3_decide`, mapping every currently-non-none
ordinal grade to each extreme. This is the pessimistic-bound discipline the ADR asks for, and the
number to reason about is the WORST case.

Population: **1,396** plan-v3 findings have `divergent_implementation` graded non-none (of 18,085).
Under plan-v3 they decided: 605 block / 701 advisory / 79 dropped / 11 indeterminate.

| Bound | Resulting decisions | block→non-block | non-block→block |
|---|---|---|---|
| BEST (every grade → `incomplete_enumeration`) | 249 block / 1,068 advisory / 79 dropped | 359 | 3 |
| WORST (every grade → a floor grade) | 686 block / 631 advisory / 79 dropped | 0 | **81** |

**Reading it.** The worst case adds **81 blocks** across 1,396 findings — a bounded increase, not a
flood, and far short of the 113-finding / 42-run over-fire that the ungraded blunt widening would
have produced (recorded in the ticket description). The best case shows the pressure-release valve
working as designed: if verifiers lean cosmetic, 359 findings that block today would demote to
coaching rather than any new blocks appearing (only 3 appear, from findings whose OTHER axes already
carried them near their bar).

The real outcome will sit between these, and — per ADR 0054 §3(b) — is determined by dogfooding, not
by commissioning a re-review sweep. The 79 dropped findings are invariant across both bounds, which
is the expected signature of the validity/veto drops firing upstream of impact.

**What to watch after landing** (the first plan-v4 calibration):
1. The realized distribution across the three grades. If `incomplete_enumeration` is near-zero, the
   valve is not being used and the change is behaving like the blunt widening we rejected.
2. Whether `omits_required_site` starts absorbing the class currently scored as
   `vague_directive: high` — three run-1 findings on THIS ticket took that path, which suggests the
   boundary between the two axes is not yet crisp to the verifier.
3. `--force` usage on `claim`. Per ADR 0054 §3(b) a spike is the signal that the value is wrong.

Note for the next calibrator: the plan-v3 cohort closed with this bump, so these 18,085 findings
cannot be pooled with plan-v4 scores (ADR 0036). The numbers above are the last measurement taken
against it.

compiled_state.description:
## Why

Calibration finding (2026-07-27/28), grounded in the persisted REVIEW_RESULT corpus
(51,964 verified findings; 18,085 on plan-v3):

A G6 finding on epic c4ad-a93e-0613-408f (sec-semantic-layer-2026-challenge) described a
mechanism that would NOT work — four sites branching on the literal `"s3vectors"` omitted from
the plan's scope, which would have re-embedded the whole corpus on every container boot and
routed a wipe to a LanceDB drop against Postgres. It scored `impact=0.0`, `severity=none`, and
landed ADVISORY despite `validity=0.8889`, `blocking_enabled=true`, `block_threshold=0.60`.

Root cause is NOT the threshold (0.60 is already the most permissive blocking bar in the
registry). `impact_plan` is a MAX over seven axes; the verifier graded all seven `none`, so
`max(...)=0.0`. The axes that recorded the real harm (`prod_impact: medium`,
`blast_radius: module`, `likelihood: medium`) are deliberately unread by `impact_plan` — they
are the superseded mean model's inputs, retained only for sidecar continuity.

The axis that SHOULD have fired is `divergent_implementation` ("the plan diverges from the
implementation/reality it claims to describe"). Corpus evidence that it is mis-calibrated:

- It fires on only 7.72% of plan-v3 findings, and it is the ONLY hard-override axis never
  calibrated (born in d487060b5, one line of prose, never revisited). Its sibling
  `ac_unverifiable` got a closed `Literal` + worked examples in story
  large-sleepful-needlefish; this axis did not.
- Of 1,307 findings in the "omitted scope site / unenumerated consumer" class — the family the
  axis exists to describe — it is graded `none` **1,173 times (~90%)**. 770 of those have all
  seven axes `none`, i.e. impact exactly 0.0.
- 47.7% of ALL plan-v3 findings (8,632) have all seven axes `none` → impact 0.0. This is the
  single largest population in the corpus, not an outlier.

## What

Two changes, landing together under ONE impact-model version bump (plan-v4), because the bump
closes the plan-v3 calibration cohort and we must not spend two.

### 1. Grade `divergent_implementation` by DIVERGENCE KIND (the approved fix)

Mirror the oracle-kind precedent exactly — replace the ordinal `none|low|medium|high` with a
closed `Literal` set that separates a load-bearing divergence from a cosmetic one:

- `contradicts_reality` — the plan asserts something about the code/system that is FALSE
  (a named symbol/file/behavior does not exist as described, or exists differently).
  KEEPS the 0.85 hard floor.
- `omits_required_site` — the plan's scope/file list omits a site the change provably MUST
  touch, where omitting it changes runtime behavior or leaves the goal unmet. KEEPS the 0.85
  hard floor. (This is the class the G6 finding belongs to, and the ~90%-missed family.)
- `incomplete_enumeration` — a site is omitted but touching it is optional/cosmetic (docs,
  comments, a redundant mention); the goal still holds without it. Contributes
  DIVERGENCE_INCOMPLETE_CONTRIB, BELOW every blocking threshold, and NEVER floors — coached,
  not auto-blocked.
- `none` — does not apply.

`DIVERGENCE_INCOMPLETE_CONTRIB` is pinned by test strictly below the lowest blocking
`block_threshold` (0.60), exactly as `UNDERSPECIFIED_ORACLE_CONTRIB = 0.55` is.

**Required structural change in `impact_plan` (not merely implied by "mirror oracle-kind").**
`impact_plan` today resolves every axis through `_SEV01`, which is keyed exclusively on
`none|low|medium|high`. The new symbolic grades are absent from that map, so a schema-only change
would silently score all three as `0.0` — the axis would stop firing entirely instead of flooring.
The named changes, mirroring `ac_unverifiable` / `ORACLE_GRADE01` / `_ORACLE_FLOOR_GRADES` exactly:

1. Add `DIVERGENCE_GRADE01: dict[str | None, float]` mapping `none`→0.0,
   `incomplete_enumeration`→`DIVERGENCE_INCOMPLETE_CONTRIB`, `contradicts_reality`→1.0,
   `omits_required_site`→1.0.
2. Add `_DIVERGENCE_FLOOR_GRADES = ("contradicts_reality", "omits_required_site")`.
3. EXCLUDE `divergent_implementation` from the generic `_SEV01` contribution loop and append its
   `DIVERGENCE_GRADE01` contribution instead — introduce `_PLAN_GRADED_AXES =
   ("ac_unverifiable", "divergent_implementation")` as the single name for "axes graded by a closed
   kind set", and drive both the contribution loop and the override loop off it so the two cannot
   drift apart.
4. EXCLUDE it from the `_PLAN_HARD_OVERRIDE_AXES` `_SEV01.get(...) > 0.0` check, replacing that
   with a `_DIVERGENCE_FLOOR_GRADES` membership test OR'd into `has_override`.

The hard floor stays applied LAST (after the detection amplifier), so a self-revealing divergence
still lands at or above 0.85 rather than 0.85 x 0.8 = 0.68.

The three-way split is required, not cosmetic: the corpus shows a blunt widening would route
113 findings into the 0.85 floor at once (42 of 983 runs flipping PASS→BLOCK, 4.3%), and the
LAST time this team widened a grade-blind hard floor it over-fired ~2x and had to be walked
back (calibration 3: 35.5% of plan-v2 blocks were floor-driven, `ac_unverifiable` 48.9% of
them, 56% mere specificity demands). `incomplete_enumeration` is the pressure-release valve
that precedent proves is necessary.

### 2. ADR: reject high-cost LLM-based calibration assessments

ADR 0054. Records that calibration MUST be driven by the data the gate already produces
during normal use (the version-tagged REVIEW_RESULT sidecar corpus) and explicitly REJECTS
purpose-built LLM eval suites / bulk re-review runs as the calibration instrument, on cost
grounds. Narrows ADR 0036's "A/B gate" to two permitted zero-marginal-LLM-cost forms:
(a) offline replay of the existing corpus under the candidate value, and (b) dogfooding the
candidate in normal use and observing field results. Supersedes ADR 0036's A/B clause only;
the permissive-rollout invariant, version-tagging discipline, and no-pooling-across-versions
rules all stand.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `docs/adr/0054-data-driven-calibration-no-costly-llm-assessments.md` exists, status
      Accepted, and states (a) the rejection of purpose-built LLM eval suites + bulk re-review
      as calibration instruments, (b) the two permitted A/B forms (corpus replay, dogfood +
      observe), and (c) that it narrows ADR 0036's A/B clause while leaving the permissive
      invariant and version-segmentation intact. Verified: the file exists and
      `grep -c "corpus replay\|dogfood" docs/adr/0054-*.md` returns >= 2.
- [ ] ADR 0036 carries a forward pointer to 0054 so a reader arriving at the older A/B clause
      is not misled. Verified:
      `grep -n "0054" docs/adr/0036-impact-model-rollout-and-calibration-cadence.md` matches.
- [ ] `PlanSeverityAttrs.divergent_implementation` is a closed `Literal["none",
      "contradicts_reality", "omits_required_site", "incomplete_enumeration"]` in
      `src/rebar/llm/review_kernel/verify_models.py`. Verified: a verification payload carrying
      `"low"` for that axis now FAILS to parse (pinned by test).
- [ ] `impact_plan` resolves the axis through the new `DIVERGENCE_GRADE01` map and NOT through
      `_SEV01` (per the four named structural changes above): it floors at 0.85 for
      `contradicts_reality` and `omits_required_site`, and returns
      `DIVERGENCE_INCOMPLETE_CONTRIB` (never floors) for `incomplete_enumeration`.
      Verified: unit test asserting all three, plus a test pinning
      `DIVERGENCE_INCOMPLETE_CONTRIB < 0.60` (the lowest blocking threshold in
      `criteria_routing.json`) so a future recalibration below it fails loudly.
- [ ] The target defect now BLOCKS: a regression test replays the exact recorded attributes of
      finding `fc347224733dccc6b` (validity 0.8889, G6 `block_threshold` 0.60) with
      `divergent_implementation="omits_required_site"` and asserts `pass3_decide` returns
      `decision == "block"` (priority 0.7556 >= 0.60).
- [ ] Both verifier prompts (`plan_review_verifier.md`, `plan_review_verifier_agentic.md`)
      define all three grades with a worked example each, in the same shape as the
      `ac_unverifiable` oracle-kind block. Verified:
      `grep -c "omits_required_site" src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_verifier*.md` returns
      at least 1 per file.
- [ ] The plan-review `IMPACT_MODEL_VERSION` is bumped to `plan-v4`, and legacy plan-v3/v2
      sidecars still read without error. Verified: `test_impact_model_versioning.py` pins
      updated and green.
- [ ] `enrich_operator_attested` handling is explicit and UNCONDITIONAL for the new grades: on a
      recorded operator attestation it MUST set `incomplete_enumeration` to `none` (automatic, not
      discretionary), and MUST NOT alter `contradicts_reality` or `omits_required_site` — they
      survive enrichment unchanged (mirroring the `broken_oracle` rule). Verified: a unit test
      asserting the exact post-attestation value of the axis for all three grades
      (`incomplete_enumeration` → `"none"`; each floor grade → itself).
- [ ] EVERY existing fixture that grades the axis on the retired ordinal ladder is migrated to
      the closed set — the Literal makes `"low"|"medium"|"high"` a parse error, so a missed
      fixture is a broken test, and one of them lives OUTSIDE tests/unit. Known sites:
      `tests/unit/test_a8e5_operator_attested_edge.py` (uses `"high"` as a surviving-other-axis
      fixture) and `tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_plan_review_gate.py:1282` (uses `"high"` as
      the hard-override fixture that drives its negative-control BLOCK). Verified:
      `grep -rn '"divergent_implementation": "\(high\|medium\|low\)"' tests/ src/` returns no
      matches outside the grade-split suite's own rejection test, AND `pytest tests/unit
      tests/interfaces` is green.
- [ ] Every PROMPT-side consumer of the axis is updated, not just the two verifiers. The G7
      criterion prompt (`src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_G7.md`) explicitly "maps its severity
      onto the existing `divergent_implementation` plan axis" and must name WHICH grade a
      leaf/parent divergence maps to (outside-the-contract → `contradicts_reality`; omitted
      required part → `omits_required_site`; cosmetic → `incomplete_enumeration`) and state that
      low/medium/high are invalid. Verified:
      `grep -c "contradicts_reality" src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_G7.md` >= 1. Its eval spec
      (`src/rebar/llm/eval_specs/plan-review-g7.eval.yaml`) references the axis in PROSE only and
      asserts no grade value, so it needs no change — confirmed by
      `grep -n 'divergent' src/rebar/llm/eval_specs/plan-review-g7.eval.yaml` showing only comments.
- [ ] The verifier prompts' shared preamble no longer tells the LLM the axis uses the ordinal
      ladder (a pink-elephant that would fight the new grades): the "Grade each axis
      none|low|medium|high (EXCEPT ac_unverifiable...)" line names BOTH kind-graded axes.
      Verified: `grep -c "EXCEPT ac_unverifiable and divergent_implementation"
      src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_verifier*.md` returns 1 per file.
- [ ] `make lint` and `make typecheck` pass; every touched `src/rebar` file stays under the
      800-LOC module-size cap. Verified: `make lint typecheck` exits 0.
- [ ] `docs/plan-review-gate.md` and the generated `docs/plan-review-criteria-guide.md`
      describe the new grades. Verified: the guide is regenerated from the registry, not
      hand-edited.

## Out of scope (recorded, not done here)

- The `prod_impact` floor ("Fix 2") is REJECTED — it collides with the novelty convergence
  floor (`novelty_priority_floor = 0.4`). See the evaluation comment on this ticket.
- `undecomposed` fires on 0.07% of plan-v3 findings (12/18,085) while holding hard-override
  power — a likely dead axis. Filed separately.
